ops.body:
Decision (2026-10-02, root-directed, PR #24): fresh Sprites mount a PRIVATE, pinned SquashFS (zstd) tool payload through the kernel loop driver. Replaces the earlier public-URL / `Inventory.Public()` design. No public hosting, no URL, no stripping of private plugins. - Config: `profiles.

.machine..payload: {path, sha256}`. The path is a local file resolved from the config dir, and setting it excludes `image`. - The input is opened with O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO cannot block the open. - The opened descriptor must be a regular file, have mode &0o077 == 0, and be owned by the caller. - Symlinks are followed rather than banned, because the resolved descriptor is what gets validated. - Producer: `cc-remote payload build --out FILE`. - Installs the full inventory, private marketplaces included, on a fresh labelled build Sprite. The GitHub token reaches only install's stdin. - Runs `plugins.sh verify` (full link checks) between install and `pack`, and never publishes readiness. - Packs an explicit allowlist and streams it back to a 0600 O_EXCL file whose parent must not be group/other-writable. - Destroys the builder only when its label proves this build made it. - Consumer: create streams the file over provider exec stdin. - The sha256 is verified on every acceptance path: a staged partial (which atomically replaces the canonical image under flock), a cached canonical image, and an existing mount (hashed through its loop source device). - The manifest must match the tools fingerprint, home, arch and OS. A mismatch is fatal, with no cold fallback. - The `cc-remote-payload` sprite-env service remounts at boot under the same rule, and inventory services `--needs` it. - Identity: - The configured payload sha256 is a framed input of the readiness stamp. Without a payload, the stamp bytes are unchanged. A path-only change keeps identity. - No Record field: the remote ready file already carries the stamp, so a changed SHA misses readyTools and re-stages, re-verifies and re-mounts. - The Namespace image fingerprint stays system-only, with no user tools, HomeTrees or plugin versions. - Schedule: - A prerequisites gate (`command -v` curl git jq python3 unzip xz plus the CA bundle; apt only if one is missing) runs before the lanes. - Packages, checkout and tools then run concurrently. - A nonempty profile Prepare waits on packages and tools; an empty Prepare stays fast. - Readiness publishes only after every lane succeeds. Evidence: setup-20261001/fresh-startup-92s-result.json, implement-fresh-payload-result.json, payload-root-review-requirements.json, payload-final-refuter.json, payload-transport-floor.json.
